lines.text: Bram spent the whole next morning trying to talk me out of it. He tried four different ways. He's very thorough.
Then send me instead, my lord. Or Wren. Or Oswin. Anyone who can swing a sword.
They didn't invite a sword, Bram.
And he has to go himself. A claim needs the claimer. You can't bond a people by letter.
But there's a price. Wren's hunters were gone two weeks. When they came back, I measured them. Not one had grown. Not one had slipped.
If I'm right, the moment you leave, it's the same for everyone here. Like dough in a cold kitchen. It doesn't fall. It just stops rising.
With soldiers coming.
A hundred and twelve people. Three weeks of growing, thrown away. Or a whole people in the north who might stand with us when the soldiers came.
I'm going.
Then I'll write to the Order while you're gone. Their hand, their codes. The village is quiet, and Lord Lucan is in bed with a cold.
It won't stop the warrant. Nothing will. But they won't know where you are, or what you're doing.
A cold. Very believable.
My lord, you're always cold. It's the most believable thing about you.
Then I went to the forge and asked Tobin for two things. Sledges, for the snow. And stoves, for the Skeld.
Stoves? My lord, they live in the Pale. There's no wood up there. The trees are made of ice.
That's why I want rimeglass stoves. No wood. No smoke. Just warm.
We still had a barn full of rimeglass from the White Night. Tobin said a dozen stoves in two days was impossible. Then he built them anyway, plus one thing I hadn't asked for.
Tobin. What is that?
Harpoon launcher, my lord. Just in case.
In case of what?
Something big. It's the Pale.
We left on the third morning. Wren, Oswin, Ilse, Kell, five hunters, my dog, and Dunn, who had forty stitches in his shoulder and refused to stay behind.
I can't hold a spear yet, my lord. But I can hold a conversation.
Come back, my lord. I'll keep everything exactly where you left it.
An hour past the north field, the green ended like a line drawn with a knife. Beyond it, there was only white.
From here, Warm One, nothing is warm but you. And the White does not like warm things.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter thirty, coming soon.
